findings.diagnosis: The scorer judges cuts by the right-hand fragment alone and over-penalizes high-contradiction short right fragments, causing it to shift cuts left into adjacent NPs and create tiny or predicate-only left fragments; it must evaluate the completeness and harm on both sides of a cut.
findings.evidence: 6 cases (en_us_888, en_us_767, en_us_741, en_us_419, en_us_924, en_us_105) keep a high-contra cut that kills the set. Targets avoid those cuts by keeping verbs with their complements or by preventing one-word/predicate-only left fragments.

edit.text: When judging a cut, assess harm to BOTH fragments: avoid cuts that leave an incomplete predicate or a one-word/NP-only fragment on either side; prefer keeping verbs with required complements rather than shifting the cut into neighboring noun phrases.

findings.diagnosis: The scorer allows cuts inside atomic measurement, date, and fixed temporal/location expressions, which breaks units or ranges and produces misleading standalone pieces.
findings.evidence: 4 cases (en_us_741, en_us_419, en_us_888, en_us_70) split numbers/units or tight temporal ranges (e.g., "2.2 million km2", "340 million to 500 million", "in summer Nov-Feb", "9,000 people"), and targets keep those as single units.

edit.text: Treat numerals+units, measurement phrases, date/month ranges, and fixed temporal/location expressions as atomic—do not cut inside them, since separating unit from quantity or range changes factual meaning.
